solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Each group of people outside hospital in pain

indicators.note: a word placed outside another wraps around it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each
a race is a group of people sharing descent
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Everyone in a crowd standing outside a hospital is suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of people' reads as the crowd in the scene, but it is a word for a people sharing descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a specific kind of pain, felt in the ear, so the general word stands for this example.

clue.text: Inexact poet misrepresented what is likely to happen

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A careless versifier got the forecast wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectation is a belief about the probable future, the thing anticipated.

clue.text: Part of dinner is Ottolenghi dish

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across dinner, is and Ottolenghi

explanation.surface: Part of the meal is a recipe from the celebrity chef.
explanation.walkthrough: Yotam Ottolenghi is a well-known London chef and cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish, so it is an example of a dish.

clue.text: A censored broadcast became cruder

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cut programme ended up more vulgar after editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as a TV programme being aired; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen is to make or become rougher and less refined, so the past tense means grew cruder.

clue.text: English soldiers keeping Russian fighter in exile

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: British troops are holding a Soviet warplane while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army; 'in' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is someone who has left their homeland, often for political reasons, a kind of exile.

clue.text: Loathing and passion displacing energy

indicators.note: to displace something is to move it out of its place, so a letter is taken out and set elsewhere

blocks.note: heat is intensity of feeling, passion
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Hatred and fervour have pushed out someone's vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of HEAT is lifted out of its place and put back at the end, turning HEAT into HATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate and loathing are synonyms for intense dislike, both usable as nouns.

clue.text: Progress by one member reduced aspiration

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a hope is an aspiration

explanation.surface: Someone's ambition shrank one step at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: One member is one leg; to hop is to move along on a single leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping is moving forward by jumping on one foot, so one limb carries you.

clue.text: Abusive poster first to target list of people?

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: opening letter of target
a roll is a register of names

explanation.surface: An online troublemaker picks out people on a list to attack first.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is someone who posts offensive or provocative messages on the internet.

clue.text: Trattoria serves this awful tapas

indicators.note: something awful is in a mess, so the letters of the word beside it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian restaurant dishes up truly dreadful Spanish snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites thinking the trattoria serves tapas; in fact tapas is just the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an Italian eatery, and pasta is the staple dish such places serve.

clue.text: Devil learning to pray

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
lore is accumulated knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A demon is being taught how to say prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray in the old sense is to beg earnestly, which is what implore means.

clue.text: Unusually rare moth, the personification of fertility and life

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters appear in an altered order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An uncommon insect is seen as the embodiment of nature's bounty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' belongs to the letters, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the Earth Mother is a goddess who embodies fertility and the life-giving earth.

clue.text: Finally slept on firm bed

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the following word, keeping only its closing letter
in an across answer one thing on another is simply written after it

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the closing letter of slept

explanation.surface: At last someone got some sleep on a hard mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: The firm piece comes first in the grid because the slept letter is placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cot is a small bed, typically for a baby, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Person unknown steals large choker

indicators.note: a thief who steals takes something and holds it inside, so one piece is carried within another

blocks.note: a stranger is someone you do not know
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An unidentified thief makes off with a big necklace.
explanation.walkthrough: A choker looks like jewellery here, but it is someone who chokes people.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler throttles a victim, so he is literally one who chokes.

clue.text: Woman taking charge of issue?

blocks.note: surface reading: a woman handling some matter or problem
setter's reading: issue means offspring, so this is a woman employed to look after children

explanation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a problem to be dealt with, but in law and old usage it means children.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic servant who cares for a family's young children fits a woman minding someone's offspring.

clue.text: Quantity for each increase

blocks.note: as in 'ten pounds a head', a means per or for each
to mount is to grow or increase, as costs mount

explanation.surface: A volume quoted per item goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity or total of something, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Squatting position starts to cause rashes that hurt

indicators.note: starts point to the opening letters, so the beginnings of the next two words are kept

blocks.note: opening letter of cause
opening letter of rashes
ouch is what you exclaim when something hurt you

explanation.surface: Sitting on your haunches can bring on painful skin irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouch is a low bent-knee posture, which is exactly a squatting stance.

clue.text: Fresh reports increase appointments

blocks.note: to up is to increase, as in up the price
dates are fixed appointments

explanation.surface: New bulletins show more meetings scheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: Updates are the latest pieces of information, so they are new briefings.

clue.text: Deal with stock?

blocks.note: first meaning: to manage or cope with
second meaning: the grip of a tool or gun, as a stock is

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shopkeeper managing inventory; stock is in fact the part you hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for coping with something and a noun for the part of an object you grip.

clue.text: Urgent item actively plugged by TV and radio?

indicators.note: acting busily stirs things up, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
something plugged has a stopper pushed into it, so another piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
television and radio are broadcast media

explanation.surface: A pressing story is being heavily promoted on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actively' reads as describing the promotion, but it only tells you to stir the letters of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immediate demands action at once, the sense of urgent as in an urgent need.

clue.text: Headgear that makes a comeback in wintertime

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the following word
coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters inside wintertime

explanation.surface: A hat style returns to fashion during the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed hat worn by bishops, a piece of ceremonial headwear.

clue.text: University dons perform in small ensemble

indicators.note: to don is to put on, as clothing, so one piece is wrapped in another like a garment

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
to do is to perform, as in do a play

explanation.surface: College lecturers play together in a little band.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like academics, but the word is a verb: U puts DO on around itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of performers, the smallest possible musical group.

clue.text: Spotted famous hosts in charge

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: noted means well known or famous
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A celebrity was seen entertaining the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed and spotted both mean saw or observed, as past-tense verbs.

clue.text: Cold, very large island

blocks.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A chilly, enormous isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos, also spelt Kos, is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: A long letter

blocks.note: taken as written
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Reads like a lengthy piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A long letter' suggests an epistle; long is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the alphabet character H.

clue.text: Fresh information points in different directions

blocks.note: north, east, west and south are the four compass points

explanation.surface: New facts are pointing every which way.
explanation.walkthrough: The four compass points each face a different way, and their initials run together.
explanation.definitionFit: News is newly received information about recent events.

clue.text: Close American emergency room receiving customer

blocks.note: the close of something is its end
US is the abbreviation for American, as in US forces
ER is the American abbreviation for emergency room

explanation.surface: A nearby US casualty department admits a patron.
explanation.walkthrough: Close looks like an adjective meaning nearby, but it is the noun meaning finish.
explanation.definitionFit: An end user is the final consumer of a product, a kind of customer.
